reason: The UPHELD verdict survives, but three of the claims behind it are wrong or incomplete. (1) The finding mixes two files. The bronze range 0.629-0.754 is from r34/mc34_vpub87a.txt, where the pair is below P3 in 6 of 6 runs (P3 0.709-0.783). The '5 of 6, exception CMODE=norm 0.862 vs 0.851' is from r34/mc34_allpartners.txt. Together: below P3 on bronze in 11 of 12 runs. (2) The finding does not mention silver. {exp87a, exp85a} is ABOVE P3 on silver in 12 of 12 runs (for example 0.572 vs 0.538, 0.709 vs 0.645, 0.496 vs 0.473), and it is at or above P3 on E[value] in 3 of 12. (3) 'Below {exp87a, exp89u} by 0.04-0.10 in 6 of 6' is wrong for CMODE=norm, where the margin is 0.001 (0.862 vs 0.863). Why the verdict still holds: the pre-registered finals objective is P(private > raw x138) first and silver second (CONTEXT l.1895), and bronze is the model's proxy for the first. The structural point does not depend on the Monte Carlo model. Both files carry cap 6 and K (the JT values, selected on the public embryo), so the pair insures only CI: +0.001 on public, private prior mean +0.0002. The user agreed to the plan (16:32Z). Nothing is built or submitted, so there is no feasibility cost.
